text:
IncidentBot: Paging on-call: p99 latency spike detected for /v1/stream (hosted-prod-us-west). p95 ~ 450ms -> 1.8s, p99 ~ 1.2s -> 3.6s. Error rate stable. Customers may report streaming stalls. @Maya you're oncall.

Maya O'Neil: I see the page. Looking at dashboards now. Is this correlated with any deploy?

Rick Tran: No deploys in last 30m per deploy-bot. I pulled traces; lots of long tail stuck in "batch_wait" scheduler stage. Suspect continuous-batching path holding open large batches while streaming requests wait.

Sara Li: Confirming traces: many requests show enqueue->batch_wait time ~2-3s, and then token generation is normal. Also high variance in sequence lengths — a mix of tiny chat pings and very long docs hitting same batcher.

Maya O'Neil: Which pool is hit? dedicated-hosting-prod-3?

Rick Tran: Yes, pool A (gpu-nv4b-prod-3). Batcher config: max_batch_size=64, max_latency_ms=2000, scheduler=fairshare. Mixed seqlen distribution recently shifted — likely because two customers (one enterprise ingest flow) started long context jobs.

Jess Ortega: Customer success flagged a couple of streaming sessions with rebuffering. Max C. said they saw multiple stalls during interactive demos.

Max C.: yup, we got 3 separate tickets in the last 20m. Two are high-value customers on Dedicated. Asking for ETA and whether their traffic can be exempted.

Maya O'Neil: Short mitigation plan: 1) reduce max_batch_size for streaming route 2) force preemption of very long seq requests to separate queue 3) enable immediate fallback to lower-latency model variant for streaming. I'll start with (1) and (3).

Rick Tran: On it. Pushing live tweak to batcher settings for route /v1/stream (pool A). Command I'm running: 
```
POST https://infra-api.internal/v1/batcher/config
{ "pool": "gpu-nv4b-prod-3", "route": "/v1/stream", "max_batch_size": 16, "max_latency_ms": 500 }
```

Rick Tran: Applying now... response OK, new config commit id: cfg-20260314-032.

OpsBot: Config commit cfg-20260314-032 applied to gpu-nv4b-prod-3 (/v1/stream). Rolling to 10% nodes -> 50% -> 100%.

Sara Li: Watching telemetry. p95 dropped to ~540ms after 20s on rolled nodes, p99 trending down but still elevated ~1.5s.

Maya O'Neil: Enabling streaming fallback to low-latency variant (quantized model q4f) for sessions that exceed queue_time > 300ms. Rick, can you add rule?

Rick Tran: Adding policy: 
```
POST /routing/policies
{ "name": "stream-lowlat-fallback", "condition": "queue_time_ms>300 && route=='/v1/stream'", "action": "route_to: model-q4f-stream" }
```
Policy created id rp-77. Deployed.

Rick Tran: Policy active. Immediately started routing ~12% of streaming requests to model-q4f-stream. Those have p99 ~ 400ms.

Sara Li: System p99 now ~1.0s and trending lower. Tail still visible in some shards. Investigating fairness algorithm interaction with mixed seq length buckets.

Maya O'Neil: Any customer impact still live? Max C.?

Max C.: After the fallback we saw degradation reduce. Two customers still had 1 degraded session each but overall support volume dropped. Thanks.

Jess Ortega: Noting to update SLT and CS: we applied temporary batching constraints and a fallback model. We'll follow up with permanent plan.

Maya O'Neil: Can runtime team look into more deterministic scheduling for mixed-seqlen? Rick/Sara, please propose follow-ups: 1) per-seqlen bucketing with stricter latency SLO 2) preemptive eviction thresholds 3) tune fairshare weights for streaming-sensitive routes 4) per-customer rate isolation for long-context jobs.

Rick Tran: I'll draft RFC and include perf numbers. Early note: per-seqlen bucketing reduces p99 by ~30% in local sim for same throughput.

Sara Li: I'll run a backtest of fairshare tweak and check paging thresholds so we don't get noisy paging.

Maya O'Neil: Handoff to Night Oncall @ 1769822345. Current status: configs applied, fallback active, p99 ~900ms trending down, customer impact limited to isolated sessions. Ops doc updated.

Maya O'Neil: Handoff summary: actions taken (batch_max_size->16, max_latency_ms->500, enabled stream-lowlat-fallback rp-77), monitoring watchlist (p95/p99 per-pool, queue_wait_histograms, fallback-rate), next steps (RFC for per-seqlen bucketing, adjust fairshare, customer isolation). If it resurfaces escalate to eng-runtime and SRE.

Rick Tran: tagging follow-ups: rfc/ops/1769812345-batching-tail (WIP).

OpsBot: Handoff recorded for oncall shift change at 1769822345.

Maya O'Neil: Leaving channel, paging suspended. :white_check_mark:
